greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Peace be with you as we gather this day to honor Christ our King, who reigns not from a throne of gold, but from the throne of the Cross and the victory of the Resurrection.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the Good Shepherd who seeks out the lost: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the firstfruits of the dead, restoring all things to the Father: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you invite us to serve you in the least of your brothers and sisters: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.
homily:
We often think of a king as someone who sits behind high walls, shielded from the dust and the heat of the road, commanding from a distance. But the King we celebrate today, the King of the Universe, is defined by a very different posture. He is the one who walks the dusty paths, who carries the lost on his shoulders, and who sits not on a distant throne, but among the sheep. Look at the image Ezekiel gives us: the Lord God himself, searching. 'I myself will look after and tend my sheep.' He does not send an emissary; he does not delegate the care of his children to someone else. He comes himself. He finds us in the dark, cloudy places where we feel scattered, and he brings us home.

Think of the way Benjamin Vo moved through his own life. He was a boy who understood that the world was a system to be known, a place where things were meant to work, to fly, and to thrive. He was a boy who looked at the horizon and saw not just a distance, but a destination. He was a boy of 'con chim airlines,' a boy who loved the mechanics of flight, who understood that to get from one place to another, you need a steady hand at the controls and a clear vision of where you are going. Ben was a boy who lived with a profound, quiet curiosity, always looking for the next piece of knowledge, the next line of code, the next discovery. But beneath that brilliant, analytical mind was a heart that knew its Shepherd. He was a boy who understood, in the simplest ways, that life is a journey we take in the company of those we love.

Let us speak the truth plainly before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who carry the weight of these five months: the house is quiet. The routines that once marked your days—the shared dreams, the laughter, the sight of his shoes by the door—are now memories that catch in the throat. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ambush of sorrow when you least expect it. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be 'strong' for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go. 

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s suffering. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus speaks of the final judgment, and he says something that changes everything: 'Whatever you did for one of the least brothers of mine, you did for me.' This is the hinge of the mystery. We think our lives are small, limited by time and space. But in the eyes of the King, every act of love is a coin invested in the Kingdom. Think of Benjamin’s heart—that boy who, unprompted, wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. That is the currency of heaven. That is the love that does not die. It is the love that continues to work in the world, just as the 'Well of Love' in Cà Mau now brings life to those who were thirsty. Ben’s love is not a memory; it is a current that keeps flowing, a grace that keeps giving.

Consider the image of the Shepherd again. He is the one who binds up the injured and heals the sick. He is the one who promises that, at the end of the age, he will destroy the last enemy: death. This is the promise of the Resurrection. Ben is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven, standing alongside the saints, fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced by the Father. He is the boy who loved to dream, the boy who giggled at the idea of his own airline, the boy who looked at the world with such profound curiosity. He is all of that, and he is with the God of the living. He is the firstfruits of the promise, waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the shared laughter, the way you both navigated the world together. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The King of the Universe is the one who is with you right now in this very room, in the silence, in the ache, and in the hope that refuses to die. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the blessing of Almighty God, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, descend upon you and remain with you always, bringing you the peace that surpasses all understanding. Go in the peace of Christ.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light of Christ the King, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve, that the Good Shepherd may console them with his presence and fill their hearts with the hope of eternal reunion, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Thus says the Lord GOD:
I myself will look after and tend my sheep. 
As a shepherd tends his flock
when he finds himself among his scattered sheep,
so will I tend my sheep.
I will rescue them from every place where they were scattered
when it was cloudy and dark. 
I myself will pasture my sheep;
I myself will give them rest, says the Lord GOD. 
The lost I will seek out,
the strayed I will bring back,
the injured I will bind up,
the sick I will heal,
but the sleek and the strong I will destroy,
shepherding them rightly.

As for you, my sheep, says the Lord GOD,
I will judge between one sheep and another,
between rams and goats.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1) The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
In verdant pastures he gives me repose.
R. The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.
Beside restful waters he leads me;
he refreshes my soul.
He guides me in right paths
for his name's sake.
R. The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.
You spread the table before me
in the sight of my foes;
you anoint my head with oil;
my cup overflows.
R. The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.
Only goodness and kindness follow me
all the days of my life;
and I shall dwell in the house of the LORD
for years to come.
R. The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Christ has been raised from the dead,
the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. 
For since death came through man,
the resurrection of the dead came also through man.
For just as in Adam all die,
so too in Christ shall all be brought to life,
but each one in proper order:
Christ the firstfruits;
then, at his coming, those who belong to Christ;
then comes the end,
when he hands over the kingdom to his God and Father,
when he has destroyed every sovereignty
and every authority and power. 
For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. 
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
When everything is subjected to him,
then the Son himself will also be subjected
to the one who subjected everything to him,
so that God may be all in all.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples:
"When the Son of Man comes in his glory,
and all the angels with him,
he will sit upon his glorious throne,
and all the nations will be assembled before him. 
And he will separate them one from another,
as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. 
He will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left. 
Then the king will say to those on his right,
'Come, you who are blessed by my Father. 
Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. 
For I was hungry and you gave me food,
I was thirsty and you gave me drink,
a stranger and you welcomed me,
naked and you clothed me,
ill and you cared for me,
in prison and you visited me.'
Then the righteous will answer him and say,
'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you,
or thirsty and give you drink? 
When did we see you a stranger and welcome you,
or naked and clothe you? 
When did we see you ill or in prison, and visit you?'
And the king will say to them in reply,
'Amen, I say to you, whatever you did
for one of the least brothers of mine, you did for me.'
Then he will say to those on his left,
'Depart from me, you accursed,
into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you gave me no food,
I was thirsty and you gave me no drink,
a stranger and you gave me no welcome,
naked and you gave me no clothing,
ill and in prison, and you did not care for me.'
Then they will answer and say,
'Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty
or a stranger or naked or ill or in prison,
and not minister to your needs?'
He will answer them, 'Amen, I say to you,
what you did not do for one of these least ones,
you did not do for me.'
And these will go off to eternal punishment,
but the righteous to eternal life."

day: The Solemnity of Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
